questions.explanation: Use There is with a singular noun.
Use There are with plural nouns.
Questions with a singular noun start with Is there.
Questions with plural nouns start with Are there.
Use There were with plural nouns in the past.
questions.q: ___ a lot of people at the party.

questions.explanation: Use There was with a singular noun in the past.
questions.q: ___ a car in the street yesterday.

questions.explanation: Milk is uncountable, so use There is.
Use There are with plural nouns.
Use There are with plural nouns.
Use There is with a singular noun.
questions.q: ___ a big tree in front of the house.

questions.explanation: Use There were with plural nouns in the past.
questions.q: ___ many students in the class yesterday.

questions.explanation: Use There is with a singular noun.
Use There are with plural nouns.
Past questions with a singular noun start with Was there.
Past questions with plural nouns start with Were there.
Two books is plural, so use There are.
options: Is there two books on the desk?
There are two books on the desk.

questions.explanation: Last night needs the past: There was.
options: There was a party last night.
There is a party last night.
There were a party last night.
There be a party last night.

questions.explanation: A bank is singular, so the question starts with Is there.
options: Is there a bank near here?

questions.explanation: Many people is plural, so use There were.
Rain is uncountable, so use There is.
options: There are a lot of rain today.
There be a lot of rain.
There were a lot of rain today.
There is a lot of rain today.
